Records only, unless brief 1.4 reached main without the test changes item 4 names: no file the site, the server or the browser tests build from changes. Keep the words "draft pull request 108" in the header (test/unit/redesign-status-step23.test.ts pins them there) or move that pin as well.

2. The record tests that move. test/unit/redesign-status-step32.test.ts pins the pending wording: its header test (the merge pending, "draft pull request 108", no commit hash in backticks) and its Checkpoint D test ("**Not merged yet: the merge into `main` is pending** (draft pull request 108)" and no "Merged into `main` as"). Both now pin the merged wording; every other pin in the file stays as it is.

3. The date line. Nine record tests (steps 24 to 32) pin that it opens "(WS01, step 32: ..." and steps 21 and 32 check that the file's first 400 characters name their steps. So keep WS01's part first and word for word, add "checkpoint D is merged" at its end, and put WS02's part after it, latest step first ("; WS02, step 1: ..."). 5. Open the WS02 section. slices.name: ws02-02-nav-model-switches-and-signed-in-harness
slices.brief:
Groundwork every chrome step uses: the navigation model, the switches its rows read, the one condition the whole chrome shows under, and a way for the browser tests to draw a signed-in visitor. Nothing a visitor sees changes; the new files are read only by tests until step 5.

src/lib/nav.ts (new), pure and typed: the one source the header, the About menu, the My LCA menu, the sheet, the tabs, the footer, the trust line and search read (WS02, Frontend).
- One entry per destination with its id, its one label (Nav-IA-Final, section F: "Board & regions", "Bylaws & rules", "Minutes", "State champions", "Scholastic", "Contact", "Clubs", "LCA on Facebook ↗", "Website help"), its address, whether it leaves the site, and the switch that makes it live.
- The six sections in order (Tournaments, Clubs, Scholastic, News, Membership, About) with the routes each owns, for aria-current and the sheet's "You are here".
- The About rows with their addresses by switch: Board & regions, Bylaws & rules and Minutes open /about/board, /about/bylaws and /about/minutes once newAbout is on, and State champions /about/champions once newNews is on; until then today's /governance/board, /governance/bylaws, /governance/minutes and /champions. Donate's place as the About menu's last row when squeezed, and the footer row "LCA on Facebook ↗".
- The My LCA rows as a pure function of what the person holds: the role, the seats and managed clubs getMySeats gives, the events they direct and their children, and later (step 17) the to-dos, the event line and the membership card. While myLcaRail is off it gives today's role rows as useAccountLinks() in Navbar.tsx gives them (Workspace, Board inbox and My region's clubs, by role); with it on none of them, and the word Workspace in no row. One Admin row: "Admin" for lca_admin, "Admin (view only)" for lca_officer and lca_observer (OBSERVER_ROLES in src/areas/admin/roles.ts).
- The sheet's order, the four tabs with their icons (the first two are the Tournaments and Clubs entries themselves), the footer's four columns by id, the hideTabBar routes as today's site has them (/tournaments/:id/print, /membership/success, /donate/success; registration, checkout, the hall TV and scanner capture join with their workstreams), and the pages and synonyms search matches on the client (parents' words from DESIGN_REPLAN_phase0.md, Q5, and region aliases such as NOLA, Northshore and Acadiana).
- An entry that waits for another workstream is live only with its switch: Calendar and This weekend with newTournaments, Results and the Champions tab with newNews, the About tabs with newAbout, Membership card with newMembership, Suggest a club with newClubs, the short menu with myLcaRail.
- One condition for the whole chrome: everything newNav turns on shows only when newLook is on as well, as the heritage look shows only with newLook (themeHeritage's comment says so). nav.ts exports it (for example chromeOn: newNav and newLook both on), every later step reads it, and siteSearch, eventStrip (with eventStripLive) and liveMarker draw only while it holds. The new chrome is drawn in WS01's tokens, dark mode and focus rings, which exist only under newLook, and without newLook the gold-ink token is brand gold #c8a94a, which on the chrome's light menus would be gold words on a light ground (0.1 rule 6). With newNav on and newLook off the site keeps today's header and footer. This is the plan's default for open question 8, recorded as a deviation; "the chrome on" in every later step means this condition.

src/lib/features.ts gains the five switches nav.ts reads that later workstreams own, each off: newAbout (WS14), newNews (WS10), newMembership (WS12), newClubs (WS09) and myLcaRail (WS13), named as brief 1.4's switch table names them. Each has a plain JSDoc comment of five words or more saying what it will turn on and that, until that part ships, it only re-points rows of the new header and menus, so it stays off until then. test/unit/test-setup.test.ts (lines 93 to 99) reads every comment after "// Redesign, Phase 0" and fails on a workstream named by its number ('WS' and two digits), on 'slice', 'builder' or 'scout', on US Chess's old initials and on an em dash, so a comment names the part ("the new About page"), never its workstream. The comments of siteSearch, eventStrip and liveMarker gain one sentence each: it shows only with newNav and newLook on. test/unit/features.test.ts holds the five off in a list of their own. A unit test fails when one of them is on while what it re-points to is missing: a route its rows open is not in src/App.tsx, and for myLcaRail, which opens no route of its own but takes Workspace, Board inbox and My region out of the menu, while /workspace/lookup (the rail's Member lookup) is not a route there. So no pull request turns one on early.

The browser harness for the new chrome:
- test/a11y/global-setup.ts: the a11y-on build turns on newNav, siteSearch, eventStrip, eventStripLive and liveMarker beside newLook and themeHeritage. The brief names newNav and siteSearch; the strip in every state and the Live tag need the other three, drawn from stubbed answers. The a11y-off build and test/a11y/baseline.json do not change. Move every pin of the a11y-on list, in both its forms: the string 'newLook,themeHeritage' in global-setup.ts line 73, and the arrays a search for that string misses, test/a11y/builds.spec.ts line 22 (SWITCHES_ON = ['newLook', 'themeHeritage']) and test/unit/scopes-edges.test.ts line 109 (the split list held to exactly ['newLook', 'themeHeritage']). The scopes-edges pin is WS01's (the AC1 matrix reads its looks on the build that turns themeHeritage on): it becomes a check that newLook and themeHeritage are among the build's switches, while test/a11y/builds.spec.ts holds the whole list. test/unit/feature-overrides.test.ts line 20 and test/unit/heritage-edges.test.ts line 424 use the same string as the flags of builds of their own, not as the list, and stay.
- A signed-in visitor in a file of its own (for example test/a11y/signedIn.ts, so support.ts stays as WS01 left it): before the page loads it plants a session for the build's fake sign-in address (http://127.0.0.1:9) in localStorage and answers GET /api/me, GET /api/board/my-seats, GET /api/me/event-mode and GET /api/live/now in the browser from a persona. Nothing reaches a real sign-in service and no server check is loosened.
- One persona list both suites read (for example test/unit/fixtures/navPersonas.ts): signed out, an active member, a member within 30 days of expiry, an expired member, a parent of two, the TD of one event, a club rep, a regional representative, an LCA officer, the president (lca_observer), an LCA admin, and one person holding all of these.
- A short spec proves the helper on today's header: signed in as each persona the bar shows Profile and Log out, and no request leaves the local server.
- Nothing new is drawn on a11y-on yet. From step 3 on the chrome's steps change what its specs read, and step 4 first moves those reads into one helper.

Standing rules for this step: every change a visitor would see waits for its switch, which stays off; test/a11y/baseline.json does not move; plain words, "US Chess", a weekday on every date, "7:00 PM", ½ for half points, and no em or en dash in code, copy, tests or records; the record calls this work "WS02 step N" (headings "### WS02 step N: ...", tags "(WS02 step N)") and never uses the working words the record tests ban; this step's record test reads only the WS02 section and the lines the step wrote, never every table row or heading in the file; every pin in another test that the step moves (an exact list, a count or a line number) is listed under its files with the change and the reason, and where the pin holds closed history, WS01's figure is kept apart from the live one rather than rewritten.

sequencing_rationale:
WS02 builds the site's frame: the header, the tablet and phone bars, the footer, search, the personal event strip and the My LCA menu, every visible part behind switches that stay off (newNav, siteSearch, eventStrip, eventStripLive and liveMarker) and shown only with newLook on as well (the chrome's one condition, step 2, a default for K). It is nineteen steps on one branch, redesign/ws02-navigation, merged in five checkpoints whose letters carry on from WS01's A to D. No step adds a table or a column (WS02's Data model is none), so no checkpoint migrates anything; if a step finds it needs one, it takes the next free number on its branch (0055 today) and the plan is looked at again.

Part 1 (steps 1 to 5, checkpoint E) lays the ground and builds the desktop header:
- the record first: checkpoint D's merge, brief 1.4's test changes if pull request 106 left them, and WS02's section opened with every criterion and decision mapped to its step, so each later step fills in a line that already exists
- the navigation model, src/lib/nav.ts, which every bar, menu and list reads, with the five switches its rows read, the chrome's condition and the browser tests' signed-in visitor; without that visitor no signed-in state can be tested on the test servers, whose sign-in service is a fake
- the page frame: the skip link, the loading line, theme-color, the chrome's own focus rings, the banners' ring on gold, and the @source not lines, WS02's first change to src/index.css
- the browser specs' reads of the header and the footer moved into one helper, measured in planning at 56 and 75 lines of code in 11 specs, so the header's step does not carry that rework
- the desktop header, with the About menu, the utilities, the squeeze and --header-h, and today's header below 1024 pixels until step 6
With every switch off this part changes only the stylesheet's size and the screen-reader state of today's header links; with newLook on as well, the page's theme-color follows an Appearance pick and the banners' focus ring on gold turns navy.

Part 2 (steps 6 to 8, checkpoint F) makes every width whole: the Menu sheet with the tablet header and the phone's app bar first, so the Menu tab has something to open; then the tab bar and the bottom dock; then the footer. After F the whole static chrome exists behind newNav, and the criteria that need all four surfaces at once (AC8, AC11, AC13 and AC18) are proved in the footer's step.

Part 3 (steps 9 to 11, checkpoint G) is search: the listing condition and the endpoint first, so the panel is built against real answers; then the combobox, the panel and the header's trigger; then /search, the Popular list, the US Chess row, Your tools and the speed.

Part 4 (steps 12 to 16, checkpoint H) is event mode, from the words out: the copy builder first, because the endpoint writes the "Players see" echo with the words the strip shows; then the endpoint and GET /api/me's new fields; then the hook and the desktop and tablet strip; then the Live tag with its 204 endpoint and the support form's fill; then the phone's event bar and banner, which complete the dock's criteria (AC9, AC10 and AC12).

Part 5 (steps 17 to 19, checkpoint I): the My LCA menu last among the parts, since it gathers the to-dos (from /api/me's new fields), the event line (from the strip) and the rows nav.ts gives; then the accessibility matrix over the finished chrome (AC1, AC14 and AC19), which can only measure the bar and the rings with every part in place, with /search, /contact and /support joining it; then the close-out.

Each checkpoint is a draft pull request that can merge on its own: every change a visitor would see waits for its switch, nothing migrates, and git revert -m 1 of the merge commit undoes it. What reaches production with the switches off is listed in each checkpoint's section: a smaller stylesheet and aria-current on today's header links (E); nothing (F); a public search endpoint answering only listed, public rows (G); the private event-mode endpoint, a live-now endpoint answering 204, and six new fields in GET /api/me that no page reads yet (H); nothing (I). Each section also says what newLook adds when K turns it on first: the theme-color and the banners' ring (E), and nothing for F to I, since the sized logo is drawn only by the new footer and everything else waits for newNav. G and H also set off deploy-worker.yml, since they change domain/ or functions/utils/, which redeploys the daily-emails worker; whether its own code changes depends on what it imports, which steps 9 and 13 check and record.
